title: Add scope-enforcer middleware, KMS region stamp, and compact audit indexer
author: Maya Chen

7d12e6c: add KMS region stamping hook and header propagation
c4b9f2a: introduce compact audit indexer and migration script

description:
Motivation: Provide tenant-scoped enforcement for operator requests, surface a compact audit index suitable for high-cardinality audit search, and propagate a stable but non-sensitive KMS region stamp to support downstream residency auditors. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) scope-enforcer middleware that enforces RBAC v2 scope annotations and consults an efficient decision cache; 2) kms_stamp_handler which attaches an HMACed region stamp (tenant salt) to outbound KMS calls and request-level audit headers; 3) compact_indexer implementation plus a safe backfill tool to build a compact search index for audit records.

Summary of changes and rationale: scope_enforcer.go performs request attribute normalization, evaluates RBAC policy predicates (policy_parser.go updated to parse new "scope:" annotations), and consults the local decision cache to avoid synchronous policy reads. infra/kms/kms_stamp_handler.go computes a per-tenant HMAC region stamp (no raw region identifiers stored in application logs) and propagates it as X-Redwood-Kms-Region-Stamp. services/audit/indexer/compact_indexer.go implements a small on-disk index keyed by (tenant,day,stamp) to allow quick residency-scoped queries without scanning full payloads. scripts/migrate/audit_backfill.go implements a rate-limited migrator with --dry-run and checkpointing. docs/security/scope-enforcer.md explains operator model and migration steps for Dedicated/Private customers. OpenAPI updated to document the new response headers and required permissions.

Checklist: [x] Unit and integration tests added; [x] Benchmarks for scope-enforcer path included; [x] KMS stamp is HMACed and tenant-scoped; [x] Backfill tool includes rate limit and dry-run; [x] Docs and OpenAPI updated; [x] Security review completed.

Changed areas (high-level): authz middleware, RBAC parser, KMS integration layer, audit indexer, migration tooling, docs, CI integration to run the new integration tests. See changed_files for the list.

CI and verification: Initial CI run failed on integration test (timeout on kms_test) due to test environment missing tenant salt; patched tests to inject fixed test salt and re-ran CI. Final CI summary: unit tests = pass, integration tests = pass, linters = pass, e2e (smoke) = pass. Deployment dry-run on staging with helm/values-compliance.yaml showed no diffs for existing manifests.

Review flow and decisions: Pre-merge review included requests to avoid leaking raw region IDs (converted to HMAC stamp), a performance request to use decision cache (added non-blocking cache step), and operational notes to make the backfill safe for large fleets (rate-limit, checkpointing). All requested changes were addressed in follow-up commits.

Merge details: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-20 by Maya Chen. Merge commit: a1b2c3d4e5f6. Post-merge actions: created a runbook for backfill operations, scheduled a staged rollout for Private installer pipelines with a slow canary, and opened a follow-up Linear task ENG-4380 to evaluate index retention tradeoffs.

Related tasks: ENG-4321 tracked the core design, SEC-220 tracked threat modeling for the region stamp, SUP-9876 is a support ticket requesting clearer residency signals for enterprise customers.
release_notes: Security: add RBAC v2 scope-enforcer middleware to enforce tenant-scoped operator requests; KMS: attach HMACed region stamps to KMS calls and audit headers for non-sensitive residency signaling; Audit: new compact audit index for efficient residency queries and a rate-limited backfill tool (includes --dry-run).
notes_for_ops: Backfill is destructive only in throughput terms; use --dry-run first and run at <100 items/sec for fleets >100M events/day. Tenant salts must be provisioned in staging before running integration tests. Helm values-compliance.yaml contains toggles to enable the scope-enforcer per-cluster.
